mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST monthly YoY < -5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate in at least one NBER-defined recession.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the trigger fails to fire during a NBER recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 97 for three consecutive months, coupled with a decline in retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 3% YoY, signals supply-side stress that elevates input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 97 for 3 consecutive months AND RSAFS YoY < -3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate during a supply shock event identified by a > 2 SD drop in manufacturing PMI.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) of at least 0.75 percentage points signals an emergency easing response to financial stress, which boosts risk appetite and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a Federal Reserve emergency meeting.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 300,000 coincident with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the trigger fires without a subsequent CPI inflation acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and justifies higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change > 0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not fire during a period of GDP growth above 2.5% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 1% each signals broad-based supply contraction, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not activate during a manufacturing recession (defined by two consecutive quarters of negative INDPRO growth).
